content: The development of this guideline adhered to the standard procedures established by the World Health Organization (WHO) for creating evidence-based recommendations. The planning phase involved discussions and documentation in collaboration with the Guideline Review Committee Secretariat. Additionally, a Guideline Development Group (GDG), a WHO Steering Group, and an External Review Group were formed, ensuring a diverse representation of technical expertise, geographical regions, and gender balance. All members of the GDG were required to submit declarations of interest and sign confidentiality agreements, in line with WHO's standard practices. Biographies of these members were made publicly available on the WHO website before their formal appointment. Suitable candidates for evidence review were identified, interviewed, and selected in partnership with the Belgian Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine. The development of PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome) questions was a collaborative effort involving the evidence review team, WHO, and the methodologist. These questions were refined based on feedback from the GDG and the WHO Steering Group. A planning document was submitted to the Guideline Review Committee and revised before final acceptance. WHO and the methodologist worked closely with the evidence review team to finalize the evidence review process. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, GDG briefings were conducted remotely, and the PanelVoice platform was utilized to manage evidence review data, facilitate pre-voting on Evidence-to-Decision (EtD) framework questions, and allow panelists to share new evidence. The GDG panel meeting was held virtually over two consecutive days, and the conclusions from the entire process were synthesized into the final guideline. This guideline underwent further refinement by members of the GDG, WHO Steering Group, and External Review Group before submission to the Guideline Review Committee. The references cited in the guideline include a wide range of studies and systematic reviews addressing topics such as the effects of swimming lessons, water safety training, childcare arrangements, and injury prevention programs. These studies provide evidence on the impact of interventions on drowning prevention, childhood development, and public health outcomes across various settings and populations.
